text:
Marathon Petroleum stock climbed 0.57% today to $424.36, continuing a strong two-week rally of 9.45%. The gains reflect a combination of tight refinery conditions and rising diesel demand: US refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, gasoline and diesel inventories remain lean, and diesel prices have hit record levels. While crude oil prices moved sideways this week—Saudi Arabia's offer of additional supplies via an alternative route eased fears over the pipeline attack—the real money for a refiner is the spread between what crude costs and what finished fuels sell for, which widens when refining capacity is maxed out and products are scarce.

The longer backdrop is supply tightness in diesel and heating oil, which are flowing into the transportation and logistics economy at historically high prices. A refiner that can push product out at full capacity into that environment is profitable—and that's why the stock has gained nearly 10% in two weeks despite oil prices themselves remaining volatile and geopolitically uncertain.
